name: Chandrayaan-1
outcome: Major objectives completed; contact lost on 2009-08-29
missionTimeline: 2008-11-14 · MIP released and impacted near the south pole
objective: Lunar chemical, mineralogical and photo-geologic mapping.
description: ISRO reports that the spacecraft completed its major mission objectives while orbiting the Moon; communication was lost on 29 August 2009.

scientificAchievements.title: South-polar impact-probe descent
scientificAchievements.observation: ISRO records a descent along 140° E to a location close to 89° S.
scientificAchievements.significance: Shown as a controlled impact event, not a successful landing.

surfaceEvent.label: Moon Impact Probe impact vicinity
surfaceEvent.coordinatePrecision: Approximate; ISRO describes a descent along 140° E, landing close to 89° S

name: Chandrayaan-2
outcome: Orbiter operating; Vikram landing attempt lost communication during descent
missionTimeline: 2019-09-06 · Vikram descent lost communication and hard landed
objective: Study the Moon from orbit and demonstrate a lander and rover near the south polar region.
description: ISRO reports that the Orbiter entered lunar orbit and its payloads remained operational. The Vikram lander separated, descended to about 2 km altitude, then communication was lost. The mission includes Orbiter, Vikram lander and Pragyan rover; the lander did not make a confirmed soft landing.
achievements: Orbiter reached lunar orbit and operated its payloads

scientificAchievements.title: Vikram descent outcome
scientificAchievements.observation: ISRO reported lost communication during descent; the official parliamentary response describes a hard landing within 500 m of the designated site.
scientificAchievements.significance: The marker is an approximate crash vicinity and is explicitly not a successful landing.

surfaceEvent.label: Vikram hard-landing vicinity
surfaceEvent.coordinatePrecision: Approximate; official parliamentary response places the hard landing within 500 m of the designated site

name: Chandrayaan-3
outcome: Soft landing and rover surface operations demonstrated
coordinateReferenceFrame: Not documented on the ISRO mission details page
objective: Demonstrate a safe soft landing, rover mobility and in-situ lunar experiments.
description: ISRO describes the mission's Lander, Rover and Propulsion Module and gives the prime landing site at 69.367621° S, 32.348126° E.
achievements: Demonstrated soft landing on the lunar surface
Deployed a rover to perform in-situ analysis

scientificAchievements.title: Elemental detection at the landing site
scientificAchievements.observation: ISRO reported sulfur, aluminium, calcium, iron, chromium and titanium; later observations also reported manganese, silicon and oxygen.
scientificAchievements.significance: Direct in-situ elemental measurements from the south-polar region.

scientificAchievements.title: Near-surface plasma measurement
scientificAchievements.observation: ISRO reported electron densities of about 380–600 electrons per cubic centimetre during the mission's observations.
scientificAchievements.significance: Characterizes the near-surface lunar plasma environment.

scientificAchievements.title: Lander–surface interaction
scientificAchievements.observation: ISRO reported that landing exhaust displaced about 2.06 tonnes of material over 108.4 square metres.
scientificAchievements.significance: Supports interpretation of lander interactions with lunar regolith.
